text:
Jeremy Lauzon is in Vegas to make forwards' evenings unpleasant, and he is doing it at volume: 75 hits and 30 blocked shots in 20 games, on a little over 17 minutes a night. The scoring line (no goals, one assist) is not the point, and it never really has been for a defenseman with 15 goals in 384 games before this season.

The part that should bother the Golden Knights a little is the shot share. With Lauzon on the ice at five on five, Vegas has taken 46.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and the team is 7.9 points better by that measure when he sits. The bounces have covered for those minutes so far.

His value has always lived on the penalty kill. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.9 wins above replacement last season, most of it (2.7 goals) shorthanded, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the front of the net more than you'd guess. What to watch: whether his five-on-five minutes hold up as the bounces even out.
headline: Lauzon hits everything, scores nothing, and that's the job
